question:
**Choose the correct relation: **

(i) √10 < 3.2

(ii) √11 < √12

(iii) √13 < √14
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To compare square roots and decimals quickly, simply square both sides of each relation.

(i) (√10)² = 10 and (3.2)² = 10.24 ⇒ 10 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Three relations to evaluate:

(i) √10 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Monotonicity of Square Roots

For any non-negative numbers a and b, if a < b, then √a < √b. This property allows you to compare surds directly by checking their internal radicands without finding their exact decimal values.

Square Root Estimation Formula

The square root of a non-perfect square N can be approximated quickly using the formula: √N ≈ x + (N − x²) ÷ (2 × x), where x² is the nearest perfect square to N.

Comparing Mixed Surds

To compare expressions like a√b and c√d, bring all outer numbers completely inside the root: √(a² × b) and √(c² × d). Then compare the resulting internal numbers directly.
